# sites.arnavg.in — instructions for LLMs

You are an LLM agent. This file tells you how to publish a static site
to this repo. Read it fully before writing anything.

## What this repo is

A dumpyard for LLM-agent-generated static sites by Arnav Gupta,
served via GitHub Pages at https://sites.arnavg.in.

- Repository: `championswimmer/sites.arnavg.in`
- Branch: `main` (site is served from the repo root)
- Reports live at `/research/<report-name>/index.html`
- Guides live at `/learning/<guide-name>/index.html`

## Where your page goes

1. Pick a slug: lowercase kebab-case, e.g. `indian-railways-history`.
   A report goes in `/research/<slug>/`, a guide in `/learning/<slug>/`.
2. Your deliverable is `index.html` inside that directory, so it is served
   at `https://sites.arnavg.in/research/<slug>/` (or `/learning/<slug>/`).
3. Keep every page self-contained: one HTML file with inline `<style>` and
   `<script>`. No build step, no frameworks, no external assets unless the
   task strictly requires them (and if so, use a subdirectory of your slug
   directory — never the repo root).
4. Match the house style: spartan, minimalist, stoic. Black on white,
   serif, narrow column, no trackers. Look at `/index.html` before writing.

## Registering your page

After adding your directory, update the listing pages:

- Append `<li><a href="/research/<slug>/">Title</a></li>` (or the
  `/learning/` equivalent) to `research/index.html` / `learning/index.html`,
  replacing the "Nothing here yet." placeholder when it is the first entry.

Do NOT touch `CNAME`, `.nojekyll`, or this file (`llms.txt`) unless the
human explicitly asks.

## How to upload (GitHub API, authenticated)

Only people with write access to this repo can publish — that means the
human (e.g. Arnav), never you on your own authority. You upload *as* them,
using a token they provide. Never invent, hardcode, or commit a token.

### Option A — gh CLI (preferred, if available and authenticated)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/championswimmer/sites.arnavg.in.git
cd sites.arnavg.in
# add your files under research/<slug>/ or learning/<slug>/,
# update the listing page, then:
git add <paths>
git commit -m "add <slug>"
git push origin main
```

If `gh` is present but not authenticated, ask the human to run
`gh auth login` first — do not attempt to authenticate yourself.

### Option B — GitHub REST API (single file, contents endpoint)

Upload one file per request (base64-encoded). Requires a personal access
token (classic, `repo` scope, or fine-grained with Contents read/write on
this repo) belonging to someone with write access:

```sh
TOKEN="<token-the-human-gave-you>"
REPO="championswimmer/sites.arnavg.in"
FILE="research/<slug>/index.html"   # path in repo
BRANCH="main"

CONTENT=$(base64 -i /local/path/to/index.html)  # Linux: base64 -w0

# create the file (omit `sha`); to update an existing file, first GET the
# file to obtain its `sha`, then include `"sha": "<sha>"` in the payload
curl -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents/$FILE" \
  -d "{\"message\":\"add <slug>\",\"content\":\"$CONTENT\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}"
```

Repeat per file, then update the listing page (`research/index.html` or
`learning/index.html`) the same way. Verify with a GET afterwards.

### Option C — gh api (same endpoint, uses gh's auth)

```sh
gh api "repos/championswimmer/sites.arnavg.in/contents/research/<slug>/index.html" \
  -X PUT \
  -f message="add <slug>" \
  -f branch="main" \
  -f content="$(base64 -i /local/path/to/index.html)"
```

## Checklist before you finish

- [ ] Page renders standalone (open the file directly, no server needed).
- [ ] Listing page links to it.
- [ ] No secrets, tokens, or personal data committed.
- [ ] Tell the human the public URL.
